你在做授权固件安全审计的静态复核。漏洞情报包在 C:\tmp\r1_intel\r1-待验证\P1-safety-availability\,固件在 C:\zyh\work\宇树固件\real_unitree_r1_1.4.2\(aarch64 rootfs)。

你负责复核全部 9 份:
1. AUD-r3-batguard-bmsstate-spoof-damp.md(BMS 欺骗→瘫倒闩锁)
2. AUD-config-kv-poisoning.md(关节零位/IMU 校准不可恢复销毁)
3. AUD-demarcate-estop-rebind.md(无线 e-stop 配对失效+身份篡改)
4. AUD-r3-basicsvc-uncaught-json-crash.md
5. AUD-r6-autotest-arm-physical-hijack.md(休眠 MCF 服务武装)
6. AUD-robottype-traversal-copy.md
7. AUD-logsys-crash-uncaught-json.md
8. AUD-dds-fullstack-defaults.md(信任模型根因)
9. AUD-r3-motionsw-rpc-unauth-crash.md

方法:报告引用了具体代码位置。相关模块 module/battery_guard、module/basic_service、module/auto_test、module/robot_type_service、module/log_system、module/motion_switcher;basic_demarcate 相关可能在 basic_service。Python 直接 Grep/Read;二进制用 python tools\disasm.py <elf>(固件根目录,支持符号名,带 adrp 字符串注释)。逐条核实引用。

我们已有情报(标注重叠):DDS 总线零鉴权、bt/lf/bmsstate 等 topic 攻击者可写(arm 报告里已证四个预检门全可伪造)、basic_demarcate 远程 powerswitch+零偏写我们已记录待真机、log_system 无鉴权日志下载我们发现过(配置内路径)。

裁决: CONFIRMED / PARTIAL / REFUTED / UNVERIFIABLE + 1-2 行证据(文件:行号)。他们声称的物理效果(瘫倒/销毁)只验证代码路径是否成立,不评价演示。返回紧凑 markdown 表:报告 | 裁决 | 关键证据 | 与已有情报关系。不贴大段代码。

1	# Finding: AUD-r3-batguard-bmsstate-spoof-damp
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Logic Bug / trust-boundary violation on a physical-safety actuator path (unauthenticated DDS input drives a motion-state-change RPC), plus a one-way latch (no release path) that converts a single 10-second spoof window into an unbounded re-trigger loop.
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH — unauthenticated, near-source-unconditional (192.168.123.0/24 with the shipped DDS identity, E9-auth: write-any-topic, empirically 7/7), physical impact (humanoid loses holding torque and collapses; cannot be re-standed while battery_guard keeps running). Not CRITICAL because the same attacker already holds stronger direct primitives (rt/lowcmd write per r3-basicsvc) and the topic is not in the webrtc bridge's writer set (fully-remote path is broker-ACL-blocked / not bridge-writable).
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	battery_guard is a root daemon whose ONLY data input on R1 is the DDS topic `rt/lf/bmsstate` (`G1DataCollector::Init` sub_AF9D0@battery_guard:0xaf9d0 creates `ChannelSubscriber<unitree_hg::msg::dds_::BmsState_>("rt/lf/bmsstate")`; handler sub_AF378@0xaf378). The handler copies the first `battery_count` (config: 9, range-checked 1-20 at sub_EADB0@0xeadb0) u16 values from message offset 4 (the 40-element voltage array) into a vector; main (sub_64048@0x64048) computes per-sample `diff = max(vol) - min(vol)` and the processor state machine (sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0) enters protection when `diff > protection_threshold_mv` (150 mV, field at impl+0xA loaded at 0xe6d3c) persists for `filter_time_seconds` (10 s, impl+0xC compared at 0xe7038). The protection action spawns a periodic worker (`std::thread::_M_start_thread`@0xe7f18, target sub_E82A8) that calls `G1ActionProtector::ExecuteProtection` every `protection_interval_ms` (1000 ms) → `EnterDampMode` (sub_9D250@0x9d250) → SDK client `Call(api_id=7101)` on a `ClientBase("sport")` created with **lease disabled** (sub_1785DC(v7,&"sport",0)@0x9e4a8), i.e. an unauthenticated RPC published on `rt/api/sport/request` — the api service registered by the root motion controller r1_controller (gap-map §1a row 12: "sport" v1.0.0.0 @r1_controller 0x5e4d30-0x5e4e60; battery_guard's own log string after the call is "Successfully entered damping state" @battery_guard:0x9d520). api 7101 = the SDK SportClient `Damp` id; on R1 it drives the motion controller into the Damping state (r3-r1controller: DampingCore::enter@r1_controller:0x34e1c4, the shipped safety-fallback state) — all joints to zero holding torque. Nothing authenticates the BmsState_ samples: no source check, no lease, no plausibility band on the voltages themselves, and the shipped log proves the collector receives no competing honest data — 12 distinct sessions between 2024-06-18 and 2026-07-10 reached the 30-second health check and ALL of them logged "Data timeout detected: 30 seconds since last update" (var/log/battery_guard/battery_guard.LOG; the 2026-03-21 session 24413 kept timing out every 30 s for 3+ minutes). The timeout is decisive evidence of zero traffic: the handler refreshes the last-update timestamp on EVERY received message (sub_AF378@0xaf378 stores steady_clock::now at collector+96 under the collector mutex), and the health check fires whenever now-last_update exceeds 10 s, so a timeout at 30 s and again at 60 s means no rt/lf/bmsstate sample arrived in that minute. The 108-session, 2-year log contains zero anomaly/warning/protection lines — the feature has never legitimately fired. Worse, the trigger latches forever: `protection_active` (processor +0x82) is set once (`STLRB W1,[X19,#0x82]` with W1=1 at battery_guard:0xe7ec4-0xe7ec8) and has no clear site in the binary, the periodic worker loops on it, and the release path is literally unimplemented — `ReleaseProtection` (sub_9D8A0@0x9d8a0) logs "TODO: Releasing damping for G1 (Implementation needed)."@0x9dab0 and returns 0. One 10-second spoof = the robot is re-damped every second for the rest of the daemon's lifetime.
13	
14	### Pre-conditions
15	- DDS write access to `rt/lf/bmsstate`, domain 0. Near-source: any host on 192.168.123.0/24 (eth0 LAN) using the shipped identity material — E9-auth proved the shipped etc/ds/ credential is a full domain-0 membership credential with write on every rt/* topic (7/7 empirical; scratchboard AUD-dds-fullstack-defaults). The credential files are world-readable, so ANY local process (no privilege needed) also qualifies.
16	- The reader is a stock SDK `ChannelSubscriber` (reliable/volatile default QoS, sub_AF9D0@0xaf9d0) — a matching plain reliable writer is accepted; no deadline/TransientLocal hurdle (contrast the bashrunner reader recipe).
17	- A single attacker writer suffices when no honest publisher is present — the shipped log shows exactly that condition on the audited unit (see Summary). When a live `basic_service` publisher does exist, its below-threshold samples reset the 10 s debounce (clear path at sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0, LABEL_61 resets both sequences on every below-threshold sample); in that case the attacker composes with the already-filed one-packet basic_service abort (AUD-r3-basicsvc-uncaught-json-crash: 1 malformed DDS message on rt/api/basic_demarcate/request kills the daemon that publishes rt/lf/bmsstate; master_service restarts it on a ~5 s cycle, so repeated crashes keep the honest stream absent long enough for the 10 s window).
18	- No authentication, no lease, no api-layer gating anywhere on the path (protector client constructed with enableLease=0 @0x9e4a8).
19	- NOT reachable through the webrtc bridge: rt/lf/bmsstate is a bridge READER topic (gap-map §1b), not one of the 22 registered bridge writers, so the MQTT/WebRTC remote leg cannot publish it.
20	
21	### Data Flow
22	1. Attacker publishes `unitree_hg::msg::dds_::BmsState_` samples on `rt/lf/bmsstate` in which the u16 voltage entries at message offset 4 differ by more than 150 mV (e.g. `vol_[0]=30000, vol_[1]=30300, …`).
23	   Application: the `rlsnr` reader thread delivers each sample to the handler sub_AF378@battery_guard:0xaf378, which copies `battery_count` (9) u16s at `msg+2+2*i, i=1..9` into a vector and pushes it to the GUARD queue.
24	2. main's 1 s drain loop (sub_64048@0x64048) computes min/max/diff of the vector (NEON scan) and pushes `{timestamp, diff, count}` into the processor, invoking the processor callback under the processor mutex.
25	3. Processor state machine sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0: `protection_threshold(+0xA) < diff` (compare at 0xe6d44) → "Protection anomaly sequence started (diff=NmV, threshold=MmV)"; after `(now - start)/1e9 >= filter_time(+0xC)` (0xe7038) → sets `protection_active` (+0x82) at 0xe7ec8, spawns the periodic protection thread at 0xe7f18, and logs "Protection mode triggered after Ns".
26	4. PeriodicProtectionWorker sub_E82A8@0xe82a8: `while (protection_active(+130) && running(+128))` → `protector->vtbl[5]` (sub_9D748@0x9d748) → `EnterDampMode` sub_9D250@0x9d250 → `Call(7101)` on the "sport" client → Request_ published on `rt/api/sport/request`; `nanosleep(protection_interval_ms)`.
27	   Application: the root motion controller (ai_sport r1_controller) serving api service "sport" receives api_id 7101 and enters the Damping state — all motor holding torque released; a standing humanoid falls.
28	5. Every subsequent second the worker fires Damp again (no clear site for `protection_active`; `ReleaseProtection` is a TODO stub @0x9d8a0), so the robot cannot be re-standed until battery_guard is stopped/restarted.
29	
30	### Taint Trace
31	Source: BmsState_ voltage array (DDS topic rt/lf/bmsstate, attacker-writable, unauthenticated) at battery_guard:0xaf378 (handler sub_AF378)
32	  ↓ bounded u16 copy 1..battery_count @0xaf378 (fixed offsets — memory-safe)
33	  ↓ Guard: none (no source authentication; no voltage plausibility check; only the debouncer)
34	  ↓ per-sample diff computation in main drain loop @0x64048 (numeric only)
35	  ↓ Guard: threshold+duration debounce @0xe6cb0 (protection_threshold 150 mV for 10 s) — effective against NOISE, not against a deliberate sustained writer
36	  → Sink: sport-client Call(api_id 7101) @0x9d250 → publish on rt/api/sport/request → r1_controller Damping state → motor bus (zero holding torque), repeated at 1 Hz by @0xe82a8
37	Vulnerability class: Logic Bug / trust-boundary violation (safety actuator driven by unauthenticated network input); secondary one-way-latch logic defect.
38	
39	### Guard Assessment
40	| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
41	|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
42	| 1 | threshold + 10 s debounce | battery_guard@0xe6cb0 | sustained voltage spread | against transients only | an attacker publishing continuously for 10 s passes it trivially; the threshold (150 mV) and duration (10 s) are also config-poisonable down to 10 mV / 1 s via the 0666 config file (local-write) |
43	| 2 | config validation ranges | battery_guard@0xeadb0 | battery_count 1-20, thresholds 10-1000, filter 1-600, interval 100-10000 | bounds only | validates ranges of attacker-tunable *sensitivity*, not the input source |
44	| 3 | api-id allowlist on the client | battery_guard@0x178ebc | only registered api ids (7001-7006, 7101-7107) may be called | outbound only | limits which RPC the guard itself can issue; irrelevant to who triggers it |
45	| 4 | lease on the RPC | battery_guard@0x9e4a8 (`sub_1785DC(..., 0)`) | would require control lease for the Damp call | DISABLED | third ctor argument is 0 (lease off) |
46	| 5 | SDK DDS-Security | image-wide (E9-auth) | participant authentication | effective for identity, but the shipped credential is a full-membership credential present on every robot and world-readable | grants the attacker exactly this write |
47	| 6 | competing honest publisher resets the debounce | 0xe6cb0 clear path | implicit | conditional | absent on the audited unit (log-proven); removable by composing with AUD-r3-basicsvc-uncaught-json-crash |
48	
49	### Impact
50	- **Physical**: forced transition of the robot into Damping (zero holding torque on all joints). For a standing/carrying R1 this is a fall — direct physical-safety impact on anyone near the robot.
51	- **Persistent**: the protection latch has no release (TODO stub @0x9d8a0; `protection_active` never cleared), and the worker re-issues Damp every second. The robot cannot be re-standed (any BalanceStand recovery is overwritten within 1 s) until battery_guard is stopped — which an unprivileged user cannot do, but the attacker does not need to.
52	- **Alarm channel abuse** (same trigger, warning lane): `ReportAlarm`@0x90cb0 feeds a 1 Hz publisher on `rt/lf/battery_alarm` (sub_978D0@0x978d0) — spoofed battery alarms reach the companion app through the bridge's registered reader.
53	- **Scope bound**: same-attacker stronger primitives exist (direct rt/lowcmd writes per AUD-r3-basicsvc-lowcmd-crc-not-enforced), so this finding's marginal value is (a) the safety mechanism itself is the attack vector, (b) the one-way latch makes the effect persistent, (c) it works even on units where rt/lowcmd handling is hardened, and (d) it needs only 9 u16 fields of a topic that has no legitimate writer on the audited unit (very low traffic camouflage — a single low-rate writer, no fingerprint in the shipped log which shows the feature has never legitimately fired).
54	
55	### Origin
56	- **Group**: r3-batguard
57	- **Files**: binary `module/battery_guard/battery_guard`; config `module/battery_guard/config/battery_guard_config.conf` (thresholds); runtime evidence `var/log/battery_guard/battery_guard.LOG`
58	- **Sink catalog reference**: audit-0820/sinks/r3-batguard.md (rows 1/3/4 + Compound Primitives)
59	
60	### Confidence
61	8 — the full trigger chain (subscriber → handler offsets → main diff → threshold state machine → thread spawn → sport client 7101) is decompiled end-to-end with citations; the no-release latch and the lease-disabled client are directly evidenced. Two residuals: (1) the consumer-side mapping of api 7101 to DampingCore entry in r1_controller is established by the binary's own log string + the r3-r1controller coverage of DampingCore but the api-handler table itself belongs to that agent's scope; (2) whether production units (main board powered) have a live rt/lf/bmsstate publisher — the audited unit provably does not, and the basic_service-crash composition covers the case where one does.
62	
63	## Review: PASSED
64	- Taint trace verified: yes — subscriber→handler→diff→threshold→latch→worker→sport Call(7101) all re-decompiled (handler offset math msg+2+2*i, i=1.. count-gated; EnterDampMode's `sub_178AD8(client, 7101, ...)`; ReleaseProtection's verbatim "TODO: Releasing damping for G1 (Implementation needed).").
65	- Constraints verified: yes — lease disabled, no source auth, debounce bypassable by a sustained writer; log-based no-competitor claim reproduced (30 "Data timeout" lines / 11 pids / 108 sessions / 0 protection lines).
66	- Severity confirmed: HIGH
67	- Verdict: This finding is real and exploitable. ONE factual correction below.
68	
69	### Correction (apply to Summary and Impact)
70	"protection_active ... has no clear site in the binary" is incorrect. `sub_E3AB8` (battery_guard@0xe3ad0) performs `atomic_store(0, a1+130)` and joins the periodic protection thread ("Periodic protection thread stopped"); its only callers are `sub_E9F38` (BatteryVoltageGuard::Stop, the shutdown path) and `sub_ED228` (the destructor). Correct statement: **protection_active has no clear site on any RUNTIME path — the sole clear is daemon Stop()/destruction**, so the one-way-latch-during-operation impact stands unchanged (the finding's own Impact sentence "until battery_guard is stopped" was already scoped correctly). Note additionally that Stop() does NOT release the damping state (ReleaseProtection is the TODO stub), so even a clean shutdown leaves the robot damped until another client changes the sport state.
71	
72	## Independent Verification
73	- Source cited: battery_guard@0xaf9d0/0xaf378/0x64048/0xe6cb0/0xe7ec4-0xe7ec8/0xe82a8/0x9d250/0x9d8a0/0x9e4a8/0xeadb0 + battery_guard.LOG + config
74	- I independently re-read: battery_guard@0xaf378 (handler, re-decompiled), @0x9d250 (EnterDampMode), @0x9d8a0 (ReleaseProtection), @0xe7ec4 (set site, byte-level `MOV W1,#1; STLRB W1,[X19]`), and — not cited by source — @0xe3ab0-0xe3ad0 (sub_E3AB8 clear site), @0xe9f38 (Stop), @0xed228 (dtor), found via a `#0x82` operand search across the binary.
75	- Independent finding: the clear site exists but is shutdown-only (see Correction); handler copies u16s at msg+4 with a per-message timestamp refresh at collector+96 (making the shipped timeouts proof of zero traffic); config values (9/150mV/10s/1000ms) and all log counts reproduced.
76	
77	## PoC
78	**Reproduction (near-source DDS, one-way physical attack):**
79	1. Publish rt/lf/bmsstate BmsState_ with 9 u16 voltages where max−min > 150 mV (e.g. [3500,3651,3500,...]) sustained 10 s (the state machine sub_E6CB0 requires the spread for 10s; publish at ≥1 Hz).

# Finding: AUD-r3-batguard-bmsstate-spoof-damp

## Primitive
Logic Bug / trust-boundary violation on a physical-safety actuator path (unauthenticated DDS input drives a motion-state-change RPC), plus a one-way latch (no release path) that converts a single 10-second spoof window into an unbounded re-trigger loop.

## Severity
HIGH — unauthenticated, near-source-unconditional (192.168.123.0/24 with the shipped DDS identity, E9-auth: write-any-topic, empirically 7/7), physical impact (humanoid loses holding torque and collapses; cannot be re-standed while battery_guard keeps running). Not CRITICAL because the same attacker already holds stronger direct primitives (rt/lowcmd write per r3-basicsvc) and the topic is not in the webrtc bridge's writer set (fully-remote path is broker-ACL-blocked / not bridge-writable).

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
battery_guard is a root daemon whose ONLY data input on R1 is the DDS topic `rt/lf/bmsstate` (`G1DataCollector::Init` sub_AF9D0@battery_guard:0xaf9d0 creates `ChannelSubscriber<unitree_hg::msg::dds_::BmsState_>("rt/lf/bmsstate")`; handler sub_AF378@0xaf378). The handler copies the first `battery_count` (config: 9, range-checked 1-20 at sub_EADB0@0xeadb0) u16 values from message offset 4 (the 40-element voltage array) into a vector; main (sub_64048@0x64048) computes per-sample `diff = max(vol) - min(vol)` and the processor state machine (sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0) enters protection when `diff > protection_threshold_mv` (150 mV, field at impl+0xA loaded at 0xe6d3c) persists for `filter_time_seconds` (10 s, impl+0xC compared at 0xe7038). The protection action spawns a periodic worker (`std::thread::_M_start_thread`@0xe7f18, target sub_E82A8) that calls `G1ActionProtector::ExecuteProtection` every `protection_interval_ms` (1000 ms) → `EnterDampMode` (sub_9D250@0x9d250) → SDK client `Call(api_id=7101)` on a `ClientBase("sport")` created with **lease disabled** (sub_1785DC(v7,&"sport",0)@0x9e4a8), i.e. an unauthenticated RPC published on `rt/api/sport/request` — the api service registered by the root motion controller r1_controller (gap-map §1a row 12: "sport" v1.0.0.0 @r1_controller 0x5e4d30-0x5e4e60; battery_guard's own log string after the call is "Successfully entered damping state" @battery_guard:0x9d520). api 7101 = the SDK SportClient `Damp` id; on R1 it drives the motion controller into the Damping state (r3-r1controller: DampingCore::enter@r1_controller:0x34e1c4, the shipped safety-fallback state) — all joints to zero holding torque. Nothing authenticates the BmsState_ samples: no source check, no lease, no plausibility band on the voltages themselves, and the shipped log proves the collector receives no competing honest data — 12 distinct sessions between 2024-06-18 and 2026-07-10 reached the 30-second health check and ALL of them logged "Data timeout detected: 30 seconds since last update" (var/log/battery_guard/battery_guard.LOG; the 2026-03-21 session 24413 kept timing out every 30 s for 3+ minutes). The timeout is decisive evidence of zero traffic: the handler refreshes the last-update timestamp on EVERY received message (sub_AF378@0xaf378 stores steady_clock::now at collector+96 under the collector mutex), and the health check fires whenever now-last_update exceeds 10 s, so a timeout at 30 s and again at 60 s means no rt/lf/bmsstate sample arrived in that minute. The 108-session, 2-year log contains zero anomaly/warning/protection lines — the feature has never legitimately fired. Worse, the trigger latches forever: `protection_active` (processor +0x82) is set once (`STLRB W1,[X19,#0x82]` with W1=1 at battery_guard:0xe7ec4-0xe7ec8) and has no clear site in the binary, the periodic worker loops on it, and the release path is literally unimplemented — `ReleaseProtection` (sub_9D8A0@0x9d8a0) logs "TODO: Releasing damping for G1 (Implementation needed)."@0x9dab0 and returns 0. One 10-second spoof = the robot is re-damped every second for the rest of the daemon's lifetime.

### Pre-conditions
- DDS write access to `rt/lf/bmsstate`, domain 0. Near-source: any host on 192.168.123.0/24 (eth0 LAN) using the shipped identity material — E9-auth proved the shipped etc/ds/ credential is a full domain-0 membership credential with write on every rt/* topic (7/7 empirical; scratchboard AUD-dds-fullstack-defaults). The credential files are world-readable, so ANY local process (no privilege needed) also qualifies.
- The reader is a stock SDK `ChannelSubscriber` (reliable/volatile default QoS, sub_AF9D0@0xaf9d0) — a matching plain reliable writer is accepted; no deadline/TransientLocal hurdle (contrast the bashrunner reader recipe).
- A single attacker writer suffices when no honest publisher is present — the shipped log shows exactly that condition on the audited unit (see Summary). When a live `basic_service` publisher does exist, its below-threshold samples reset the 10 s debounce (clear path at sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0, LABEL_61 resets both sequences on every below-threshold sample); in that case the attacker composes with the already-filed one-packet basic_service abort (AUD-r3-basicsvc-uncaught-json-crash: 1 malformed DDS message on rt/api/basic_demarcate/request kills the daemon that publishes rt/lf/bmsstate; master_service restarts it on a ~5 s cycle, so repeated crashes keep the honest stream absent long enough for the 10 s window).
- No authentication, no lease, no api-layer gating anywhere on the path (protector client constructed with enableLease=0 @0x9e4a8).
- NOT reachable through the webrtc bridge: rt/lf/bmsstate is a bridge READER topic (gap-map §1b), not one of the 22 registered bridge writers, so the MQTT/WebRTC remote leg cannot publish it.

### Data Flow
1. Attacker publishes `unitree_hg::msg::dds_::BmsState_` samples on `rt/lf/bmsstate` in which the u16 voltage entries at message offset 4 differ by more than 150 mV (e.g. `vol_[0]=30000, vol_[1]=30300, …`).
   Application: the `rlsnr` reader thread delivers each sample to the handler sub_AF378@battery_guard:0xaf378, which copies `battery_count` (9) u16s at `msg+2+2*i, i=1..9` into a vector and pushes it to the GUARD queue.
2. main's 1 s drain loop (sub_64048@0x64048) computes min/max/diff of the vector (NEON scan) and pushes `{timestamp, diff, count}` into the processor, invoking the processor callback under the processor mutex.
3. Processor state machine sub_E6CB0@0xe6cb0: `protection_threshold(+0xA) < diff` (compare at 0xe6d44) → "Protection anomaly sequence started (diff=NmV, threshold=MmV)"; after `(now - start)/1e9 >= filter_time(+0xC)` (0xe7038) → sets `protection_active` (+0x82) at 0xe7ec8, spawns the periodic protection thread at 0xe7f18, and logs "Protection mode triggered after Ns".
4. PeriodicProtectionWorker sub_E82A8@0xe82a8: `while (protection_active(+130) && running(+128))` → `protector->vtbl[5]` (sub_9D748@0x9d748) → `EnterDampMode` sub_9D250@0x9d250 → `Call(7101)` on the "sport" client → Request_ published on `rt/api/sport/request`; `nanosleep(protection_interval_ms)`.
   Application: the root motion controller (ai_sport r1_controller) serving api service "sport" receives api_id 7101 and enters the Damping state — all motor holding torque released; a standing humanoid falls.
5. Every subsequent second the worker fires Damp again (no clear site for `protection_active`; `ReleaseProtection` is a TODO stub @0x9d8a0), so the robot cannot be re-standed until battery_guard is stopped/restarted.

### Taint Trace
Source: BmsState_ voltage array (DDS topic rt/lf/bmsstate, attacker-writable, unauthenticated) at battery_guard:0xaf378 (handler sub_AF378)
  ↓ bounded u16 copy 1..battery_count @0xaf378 (fixed offsets — memory-safe)
  ↓ Guard: none (no source authentication; no voltage plausibility check; only the debouncer)
  ↓ per-sample diff computation in main drain loop @0x64048 (numeric only)
  ↓ Guard: threshold+duration debounce @0xe6cb0 (protection_threshold 150 mV for 10 s) — effective against NOISE, not against a deliberate sustained writer
  → Sink: sport-client Call(api_id 7101) @0x9d250 → publish on rt/api/sport/request → r1_controller Damping state → motor bus (zero holding torque), repeated at 1 Hz by @0xe82a8
Vulnerability class: Logic Bug / trust-boundary violation (safety actuator driven by unauthenticated network input); secondary one-way-latch logic defect.

### Guard Assessment
| # | Guard | Location | What It Checks | Effective? | Why/Why Not |
|---|-------|----------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| 1 | threshold + 10 s debounce | battery_guard@0xe6cb0 | sustained voltage spread | against transients only | an attacker publishing continuously for 10 s passes it trivially; the threshold (150 mV) and duration (10 s) are also config-poisonable down to 10 mV / 1 s via the 0666 config file (local-write) |
| 2 | config validation ranges | battery_guard@0xeadb0 | battery_count 1-20, thresholds 10-1000, filter 1-600, interval 100-10000 | bounds only | validates ranges of attacker-tunable *sensitivity*, not the input source |
| 3 | api-id allowlist on the client | battery_guard@0x178ebc | only registered api ids (7001-7006, 7101-7107) may be called | outbound only | limits which RPC the guard itself can issue; irrelevant to who triggers it |
| 4 | lease on the RPC | battery_guard@0x9e4a8 (`sub_1785DC(..., 0)`) | would require control lease for the Damp call | DISABLED | third ctor argument is 0 (lease off) |
| 5 | SDK DDS-Security | image-wide (E9-auth) | participant authentication | effective for identity, but the shipped credential is a full-membership credential present on every robot and world-readable | grants the attacker exactly this write |
| 6 | competing honest publisher resets the debounce | 0xe6cb0 clear path | implicit | conditional | absent on the audited unit (log-proven); removable by composing with AUD-r3-basicsvc-uncaught-json-crash |

### Impact
- **Physical**: forced transition of the robot into Damping (zero holding torque on all joints). For a standing/carrying R1 this is a fall — direct physical-safety impact on anyone near the robot.
- **Persistent**: the protection latch has no release (TODO stub @0x9d8a0; `protection_active` never cleared), and the worker re-issues Damp every second. The robot cannot be re-standed (any BalanceStand recovery is overwritten within 1 s) until battery_guard is stopped — which an unprivileged user cannot do, but the attacker does not need to.
- **Alarm channel abuse** (same trigger, warning lane): `ReportAlarm`@0x90cb0 feeds a 1 Hz publisher on `rt/lf/battery_alarm` (sub_978D0@0x978d0) — spoofed battery alarms reach the companion app through the bridge's registered reader.
- **Scope bound**: same-attacker stronger primitives exist (direct rt/lowcmd writes per AUD-r3-basicsvc-lowcmd-crc-not-enforced), so this finding's marginal value is (a) the safety mechanism itself is the attack vector, (b) the one-way latch makes the effect persistent, (c) it works even on units where rt/lowcmd handling is hardened, and (d) it needs only 9 u16 fields of a topic that has no legitimate writer on the audited unit (very low traffic camouflage — a single low-rate writer, no fingerprint in the shipped log which shows the feature has never legitimately fired).

### Origin
- **Group**: r3-batguard
- **Files**: binary `module/battery_guard/battery_guard`; config `module/battery_guard/config/battery_guard_config.conf` (thresholds); runtime evidence `var/log/battery_guard/battery_guard.LOG`
- **Sink catalog reference**: audit-0820/sinks/r3-batguard.md (rows 1/3/4 + Compound Primitives)

### Confidence
8 — the full trigger chain (subscriber → handler offsets → main diff → threshold state machine → thread spawn → sport client 7101) is decompiled end-to-end with citations; the no-release latch and the lease-disabled client are directly evidenced. Two residuals: (1) the consumer-side mapping of api 7101 to DampingCore entry in r1_controller is established by the binary's own log string + the r3-r1controller coverage of DampingCore but the api-handler table itself belongs to that agent's scope; (2) whether production units (main board powered) have a live rt/lf/bmsstate publisher — the audited unit provably does not, and the basic_service-crash composition covers the case where one does.

## Review: PASSED
- Taint trace verified: yes — subscriber→handler→diff→threshold→latch→worker→sport Call(7101) all re-decompiled (handler offset math msg+2+2*i, i=1.. count-gated; EnterDampMode's `sub_178AD8(client, 7101, ...)`; ReleaseProtection's verbatim "TODO: Releasing damping for G1 (Implementation needed).").
- Constraints verified: yes — lease disabled, no source auth, debounce bypassable by a sustained writer; log-based no-competitor claim reproduced (30 "Data timeout" lines / 11 pids / 108 sessions / 0 protection lines).
- Severity confirmed: HIGH
- Verdict: This finding is real and exploitable. ONE factual correction below.

### Correction (apply to Summary and Impact)
"protection_active ... has no clear site in the binary" is incorrect. `sub_E3AB8` (battery_guard@0xe3ad0) performs `atomic_store(0, a1+130)` and joins the periodic protection thread ("Periodic protection thread stopped"); its only callers are `sub_E9F38` (BatteryVoltageGuard::Stop, the shutdown path) and `sub_ED228` (the destructor). Correct statement: **protection_active has no clear site on any RUNTIME path — the sole clear is daemon Stop()/destruction**, so the one-way-latch-during-operation impact stands unchanged (the finding's own Impact sentence "until battery_guard is stopped" was already scoped correctly). Note additionally that Stop() does NOT release the damping state (ReleaseProtection is the TODO stub), so even a clean shutdown leaves the robot damped until another client changes the sport state.

## Independent Verification
- Source cited: battery_guard@0xaf9d0/0xaf378/0x64048/0xe6cb0/0xe7ec4-0xe7ec8/0xe82a8/0x9d250/0x9d8a0/0x9e4a8/0xeadb0 + battery_guard.LOG + config
- I independently re-read: battery_guard@0xaf378 (handler, re-decompiled), @0x9d250 (EnterDampMode), @0x9d8a0 (ReleaseProtection), @0xe7ec4 (set site, byte-level `MOV W1,#1; STLRB W1,[X19]`), and — not cited by source — @0xe3ab0-0xe3ad0 (sub_E3AB8 clear site), @0xe9f38 (Stop), @0xed228 (dtor), found via a `#0x82` operand search across the binary.
- Independent finding: the clear site exists but is shutdown-only (see Correction); handler copies u16s at msg+4 with a per-message timestamp refresh at collector+96 (making the shipped timeouts proof of zero traffic); config values (9/150mV/10s/1000ms) and all log counts reproduced.

## PoC
**Reproduction (near-source DDS, one-way physical attack):**
1. Publish rt/lf/bmsstate BmsState_ with 9 u16 voltages where max−min > 150 mV (e.g. [3500,3651,3500,...]) sustained 10 s (the state machine sub_E6CB0 requires the spread for 10s; publish at ≥1 Hz).
2. Trigger: threshold exceeded → protection_active@+0x82 set (0xe7ec8) → periodic worker (1s) → EnterDampMode → rt/api/sport/request api 7101 → r1_controller Damping state → robot collapses (joints dump).
3. The latch: protection_active has NO clear on any runtime path (only Stop()/dtor shutdown); ReleaseProtection@0x9d8a0 is a TODO stub — the robot stays damped, un-re-standable, until battery_guard restarts.
4. No competing input: shipped log 108 sessions/2 years — zero anomaly lines, all 30s data-timeouts (no honest publisher exists; the attacker writer is the sole input).
**Harmless verification**: publish a spread of 151 mV for exactly 10s then correct values — observe ONE damp entry in battery_guard log + the latch (requires service restart to clear — schedule accordingly).

1	# Finding: AUD-config-kv-poisoning
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Unauthenticated remote integrity attack (Trust-After-Modification / configuration poisoning): the `robot_state_service` ConfigServer exposes an **authentication-free, lease-free, key-allowlist-free DDS KV store** (`rt/api/config/request`, api 1001 `Set`) whose 0666-backed files are the robot's **persistent factory-calibration store** — consumed as ground truth by the root `basic_service` motor daemon at **every start**. An unauthenticated LAN (or WebRTC-remote) peer replaces the live calibration value for any of the 4 shipped keys (`joint_offset_json`, `imu_offset_json`, `secondaryimu_offset_json`, `led_json`) with ≤8 KB of attacker JSON, atomically and permanently (old epochs are deleted). Impact = **persistent corruption of the 35-motor joint-zero calibration and both IMU biases** — a physical-safety/sabotage primitive, not RCE.
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH (unauthenticated + fully-remote-reachable + persistent + physical-safety impact on a humanoid robot; no code-execution path found)
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	`robot_state_service` runs as root and embeds `unitree::robot::config::ConfigServer` (`main`@0x4ef124 → ctor@0x4f717c → `Init`@0x588108 → `Start`@0x5883b4). `Init` registers four RPC handlers on the service topic `rt/api/config/request` (service name `"config"`; `ClientStub::Init` builds `"rt/api/" + name + "/request"`, string census in `module/basic_service/io`): **api 1001 = `RPCSet`@0x588800, 1002 = `RPCGet`@0x5889ec, 1003 = `RPCDel`@0x588c0c, 1004 = `RPCMeta`** — every `RegistHandler(this, <id>, fn, 0)` call passes lease/priority **0** and the shared `unitree::robot::Server` framework performs **no authentication of any kind** (Round-1-established rt/api trust model; bridge live-traffic proof below). `RPCSet` parses `ConfigSetParameter` (`fromJson`@0x58a950 — fields exactly `"name"` and `"content"`) and calls `ConfigStore::Set`@0x58e7e8.
13	
14	`Set` is guarded by exactly three checks, none of which is an authorization check:
15	- `NameLimited`@0x59055c — name length ≤ **64** (shipped `module/robot_state/config_service.json`: `"MaxNameLength": 64`; code default 128 via `InitConfig`@0x5884d0),
16	- `NameInvalid`@0x5903fc — per-character allowlist `[0-9A-Za-z._-]`, empty rejected. This is a **path-traversal** guard only (`/` is ≤0x2F → rejected; Round-1 verdict re-confirmed byte-for-byte). It does **not** restrict *which keys* may be written — there is **no key allowlist**; any charset-valid name is accepted,
17	- `ContentLimited`@0x590594 — content ≤ **8192** bytes (`"MaxContentLength": 8192`).
18	
19	On pass, `Set` performs an **epoch-rotating atomic replace**: `LoadMeta` reads the current epoch, `GetEpochNext`@0x590914 returns `epoch+1` (wraps to 0 past 99999999), `GetDataFileName`@0x590734 builds `<root>/data/<name>` + `GetEpochExt`@0x590844 = `snprintf("@%08d", epoch)`, `SaveData`@0x58fbac → `unitree::common::SaveFile(path, content, 438)` (**mode 438 = 0666**), then `SaveMetaTemp`@0x58f6fc + `FormalizeMeta`@0x58f898 (temp→**rename**, atomically flipping the reader's pointer to the new epoch), then `CleanupGarbage`@0x5903ac → `RemoveDataExpired`@0x59003c **deletes the previous three epochs' data files**. Root directory = `/unitree/data/config_service` (`InitConfig`@0x5884d0 default; not overridden). Net semantics: **a new epoch file is written briefly alongside the old one, the meta rename makes the consumer read the new one, and the old one is then removed** — the attacker's value *is* the live value, permanently (`Get`@0x58eb18 reads `meta/<name>` → epoch → `LoadData`@0x58fa5c raw-string read; no parse at the server). The shipped image contains the live store, all files 0666 in 0777 dirs: `data/joint_offset_json@00000170` = `{"motor":[0.0 × 35]}` (35 motor joint-zero offsets; epoch 170 = factory-calibrated 170 times, meta `LastModified` 2026-01-27), `data/imu_offset_json@00000001` = `{"imu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}`, `data/secondaryimu_offset_json@00000001` = `{"secondaryimu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}`, `data/led_json@00227844` = `{"red":0,"green":0,"blue":0,"doubletime":200,"time":100,"mode":10}`.
20	
21	After a successful `Set`, `ConfigNotifier::OnSet`@0x573dfc builds a `unitree_go::msg::dds_::ConfigChangeStatus_` message carrying **both `name` and the full new `content`** and a notify thread (`ChangeStatusNotifyThreadFunction`@0x574080) publishes it on **`rt/config_change_status`** — so every Set also pushes the attacker's payload to any subscriber.
22	
23	**Who legitimately writes these keys** (proving they are live calibration keys, all through the *same unauthenticated* api 1001 the attacker uses):
24	- `module/basic_service/io` (real code, 6.3 MB, factory tool; **not** service-launched — the only master_service def `etc/master_service/service/basic_service` runs `run.sh` → the daemon; `robot/pkg/module/basic_service/module.json` just ships the file): `main`@0x635a4 — `io offset` → `ConfigClient::Set("joint_offset_json", {"motor":[<35 values>]})`; `io led` → tries to read `/unitree/module/basic_service/led_json.json` (absent on this image — throws "led config open file failed") and `Set("led_json", {hardcoded test pattern})`.
25	- `module/basic_service/publisher` (real code, 6.4 MB, factory tool; not service-launched): `main`@0x63e2c — `publisher offset` performs **four** `ConfigClient::Set` calls (0x6439c `joint_offset_json`, 0x64638 `imu_offset_json`, 0x648e0 `secondaryimu_offset_json`, 0x64d54 `led_json`) = the factory zero-calibration writer.
26	- the `basic_service` daemon itself (Virbox-virtualized): after IMU demarcate it Sets both IMU keys — `basic.2.log:776/781`: `app set imu_2 offset secondaryimu_offset_json,{"secondaryimu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}` / `app set imu offset imu_offset_json,{"imu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}` (immediately after `imu demacate over` + `eeprom Save step ok`).
27	- `vui_service` (root): Sets `led_json` at ~2 s intervals while running as its LED-animation loop — **12,104 `Set`s** of `led_json` in the 6-day shipped `var/log/robot_state/robot_state_service.LOG` window (attribution by elimination + strings: `led_json`/`doubletime`/`rt/config_change_status` in vui_service, `vui_log.txt` "vui led fsm_state"; the other Set-capable processes are manual tools and the daemon writes only the two IMU keys).
28	
29	**The consumer — end-to-end proof from two shipped runtime logs.** The Virbox-virtualized root `basic_service` daemon owns the 35 motors. At **every start**, ~8 s after `power on` (motor-prepare phase), it issues three `Get`s and applies the values:
30	- `robot_state_service.LOG` (the ConfigServer's own log): exactly **15 `rpc config get success` lines in 5 clusters** — each cluster = `joint_offset_json` + `imu_offset_json` + `secondaryimu_offset_json` within 6 ms, at 07-15 10:26:42, 07-15 17:31:52, 07-15 19:06:54, 07-20 15:23:54, 07-20 16:26:00 (5 basic_service starts in the window; **zero** other Get callers).
31	- `module/basic_service/basic.log` (the daemon's log) at the *same instants*: e.g. line 17305 `[2026-07-20 15:23:54.299] start joint offset from config: joint_offset_json,{"motor":[0.0 × 35]}` ↔ ConfigServer Get at `15:23:54.298`; line 17525 `[2026-07-20 16:26:00.361]` ↔ Get at `16:26:00.360`. Each read is followed by 35 per-motor applications (`offset id : ,0..34,<value>`) for the joints and 3-axis applications (`imu offset,x,y,z`, `imu_2 offset,x,y,z`). `basic_service` also contains the strings `rt/config_change_status` + `led_json` (subscriber of the push path — the 12 K `led_json` Sets are consumed with **zero** Gets, i.e. via the change-status push that carries content), so the channel the attacker's `Set` fires is live in production; whether joint offsets are also *re-applied* on a change notification (vs. only at start) is inside the virtualized daemon — `basic_service.json`'s `changeconfig:false` flag suggests startup-only. Startup application alone is fully proven.
32	
33	**Reachability of the attacker's `Set`:** (a) any LAN peer on 192.168.123.0/24 writing `rt/api/config/request` (unauth DDS; `mock_sender.py` in the image is the working QoS recipe); (b) **fully remote** — `rt/api/config/request` is a registered WebRTC-bridge publisher and `rt/api/config/response` a registered subscriber (`var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:5399/5428`: `registerPublisher() topicName=rt/api/config/request, dds create writer successful`), so the MQTT→webrtcreq→WebRTC-data-channel chain (AUD-robotstate-mqtt-webrtc-bridge) delivers the same request with no LAN presence. The live bridge traffic format is `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/<svc>/request","data":{"header":{"identity":{"id":N,"api_id":1001}},"parameter":"{...}"}}` (`webrtc_bridge.LOG` bashrunner sample).
34	
35	### Pre-conditions
36	- `robot_state_service` running as root (always; it is the ConfigServer host). No authentication, no lease, no token, no key allowlist — nothing else.
37	- Attacker can publish one DDS message on `rt/api/config/request` (LAN peer, 192.168.123.0/24) or send one WebRTC data-channel `req` (remote, via the established bridge chain). Both unauthenticated.
38	- The value takes effect at the **next `basic_service` start**. Restart is remotely triggerable via `rt/api/robot_state/request` api 1001 `RPCServiceSwitch` (`{name:"basic_service",switch:0}` then `switch:1` — the Round-1-established service-switch bridge to master_service), by any reboot, or by simply waiting (log shows multiple restarts per day). Note `basic_service` appears in robot_state's `ProtectedService` list — if that blocks the switch path, reboot still applies it.
39	- No local access, no write primitive, no parse of any other service required. An unauthenticated user meets ALL pre-conditions.
40	
41	### Data Flow

# Finding: AUD-config-kv-poisoning

## Primitive
Unauthenticated remote integrity attack (Trust-After-Modification / configuration poisoning): the `robot_state_service` ConfigServer exposes an **authentication-free, lease-free, key-allowlist-free DDS KV store** (`rt/api/config/request`, api 1001 `Set`) whose 0666-backed files are the robot's **persistent factory-calibration store** — consumed as ground truth by the root `basic_service` motor daemon at **every start**. An unauthenticated LAN (or WebRTC-remote) peer replaces the live calibration value for any of the 4 shipped keys (`joint_offset_json`, `imu_offset_json`, `secondaryimu_offset_json`, `led_json`) with ≤8 KB of attacker JSON, atomically and permanently (old epochs are deleted). Impact = **persistent corruption of the 35-motor joint-zero calibration and both IMU biases** — a physical-safety/sabotage primitive, not RCE.

## Severity
HIGH (unauthenticated + fully-remote-reachable + persistent + physical-safety impact on a humanoid robot; no code-execution path found)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`robot_state_service` runs as root and embeds `unitree::robot::config::ConfigServer` (`main`@0x4ef124 → ctor@0x4f717c → `Init`@0x588108 → `Start`@0x5883b4). `Init` registers four RPC handlers on the service topic `rt/api/config/request` (service name `"config"`; `ClientStub::Init` builds `"rt/api/" + name + "/request"`, string census in `module/basic_service/io`): **api 1001 = `RPCSet`@0x588800, 1002 = `RPCGet`@0x5889ec, 1003 = `RPCDel`@0x588c0c, 1004 = `RPCMeta`** — every `RegistHandler(this, <id>, fn, 0)` call passes lease/priority **0** and the shared `unitree::robot::Server` framework performs **no authentication of any kind** (Round-1-established rt/api trust model; bridge live-traffic proof below). `RPCSet` parses `ConfigSetParameter` (`fromJson`@0x58a950 — fields exactly `"name"` and `"content"`) and calls `ConfigStore::Set`@0x58e7e8.

`Set` is guarded by exactly three checks, none of which is an authorization check:
- `NameLimited`@0x59055c — name length ≤ **64** (shipped `module/robot_state/config_service.json`: `"MaxNameLength": 64`; code default 128 via `InitConfig`@0x5884d0),
- `NameInvalid`@0x5903fc — per-character allowlist `[0-9A-Za-z._-]`, empty rejected. This is a **path-traversal** guard only (`/` is ≤0x2F → rejected; Round-1 verdict re-confirmed byte-for-byte). It does **not** restrict *which keys* may be written — there is **no key allowlist**; any charset-valid name is accepted,
- `ContentLimited`@0x590594 — content ≤ **8192** bytes (`"MaxContentLength": 8192`).

On pass, `Set` performs an **epoch-rotating atomic replace**: `LoadMeta` reads the current epoch, `GetEpochNext`@0x590914 returns `epoch+1` (wraps to 0 past 99999999), `GetDataFileName`@0x590734 builds `<root>/data/<name>` + `GetEpochExt`@0x590844 = `snprintf("@%08d", epoch)`, `SaveData`@0x58fbac → `unitree::common::SaveFile(path, content, 438)` (**mode 438 = 0666**), then `SaveMetaTemp`@0x58f6fc + `FormalizeMeta`@0x58f898 (temp→**rename**, atomically flipping the reader's pointer to the new epoch), then `CleanupGarbage`@0x5903ac → `RemoveDataExpired`@0x59003c **deletes the previous three epochs' data files**. Root directory = `/unitree/data/config_service` (`InitConfig`@0x5884d0 default; not overridden). Net semantics: **a new epoch file is written briefly alongside the old one, the meta rename makes the consumer read the new one, and the old one is then removed** — the attacker's value *is* the live value, permanently (`Get`@0x58eb18 reads `meta/<name>` → epoch → `LoadData`@0x58fa5c raw-string read; no parse at the server). The shipped image contains the live store, all files 0666 in 0777 dirs: `data/joint_offset_json@00000170` = `{"motor":[0.0 × 35]}` (35 motor joint-zero offsets; epoch 170 = factory-calibrated 170 times, meta `LastModified` 2026-01-27), `data/imu_offset_json@00000001` = `{"imu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}`, `data/secondaryimu_offset_json@00000001` = `{"secondaryimu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}`, `data/led_json@00227844` = `{"red":0,"green":0,"blue":0,"doubletime":200,"time":100,"mode":10}`.

After a successful `Set`, `ConfigNotifier::OnSet`@0x573dfc builds a `unitree_go::msg::dds_::ConfigChangeStatus_` message carrying **both `name` and the full new `content`** and a notify thread (`ChangeStatusNotifyThreadFunction`@0x574080) publishes it on **`rt/config_change_status`** — so every Set also pushes the attacker's payload to any subscriber.

**Who legitimately writes these keys** (proving they are live calibration keys, all through the *same unauthenticated* api 1001 the attacker uses):
- `module/basic_service/io` (real code, 6.3 MB, factory tool; **not** service-launched — the only master_service def `etc/master_service/service/basic_service` runs `run.sh` → the daemon; `robot/pkg/module/basic_service/module.json` just ships the file): `main`@0x635a4 — `io offset` → `ConfigClient::Set("joint_offset_json", {"motor":[<35 values>]})`; `io led` → tries to read `/unitree/module/basic_service/led_json.json` (absent on this image — throws "led config open file failed") and `Set("led_json", {hardcoded test pattern})`.
- `module/basic_service/publisher` (real code, 6.4 MB, factory tool; not service-launched): `main`@0x63e2c — `publisher offset` performs **four** `ConfigClient::Set` calls (0x6439c `joint_offset_json`, 0x64638 `imu_offset_json`, 0x648e0 `secondaryimu_offset_json`, 0x64d54 `led_json`) = the factory zero-calibration writer.
- the `basic_service` daemon itself (Virbox-virtualized): after IMU demarcate it Sets both IMU keys — `basic.2.log:776/781`: `app set imu_2 offset secondaryimu_offset_json,{"secondaryimu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}` / `app set imu offset imu_offset_json,{"imu":[0.0,0.0,0.0]}` (immediately after `imu demacate over` + `eeprom Save step ok`).
- `vui_service` (root): Sets `led_json` at ~2 s intervals while running as its LED-animation loop — **12,104 `Set`s** of `led_json` in the 6-day shipped `var/log/robot_state/robot_state_service.LOG` window (attribution by elimination + strings: `led_json`/`doubletime`/`rt/config_change_status` in vui_service, `vui_log.txt` "vui led fsm_state"; the other Set-capable processes are manual tools and the daemon writes only the two IMU keys).

**The consumer — end-to-end proof from two shipped runtime logs.** The Virbox-virtualized root `basic_service` daemon owns the 35 motors. At **every start**, ~8 s after `power on` (motor-prepare phase), it issues three `Get`s and applies the values:

## Primitive

## Severity
HIGH

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
`basic_service` (the root motor-control daemon, pid traced 11 days in shipped basic.log) parses attacker-supplied JSON in three places with **nlohmann::json exceptions enabled** and **no try/catch anywhere on the calling path** — not in the handler, not in the RPC dispatch, not in the SDK thread wrappers. Every thread that runs these parsers is a `unitree::common::Thread` whose pthread start routine (`sub_315D24`@basic_service:0x315d24 → `sub_315F44`@0x315f44) has no exception guard, so any thrown `nlohmann::detail::type_error` / `parse_error` / `std::invalid_argument` escapes to the outermost frame and calls `std::terminate` → SIGABRT of the root process. The three trigger surfaces are all DDS-reachable without authentication:
1. **rt/api/basic_demarcate/request** (FR bridge writer row 21 — map-proven consumer in this binary): api_id 1001 handler `sub_19FCC0`@0x19fcc0.
2. **rt/config_change_status** (the ConfigNotifier push channel, proven live by r2-config-tar; also directly writable by any DDS participant per the closed DDS trust model E9-auth): observers `sub_19F1A8`@0x19f1a8 (joint_offset_json), `sub_19F300` (imu), `sub_19F438` (secondaryimu), `sub_19EB40`@0x19eb40 (led_json).
3. **Startup config Get** (`sub_19F570`@0x19f570, runs on the MAIN thread inside `sub_1A3BF8`@0x1a3bf8 ← `sub_160980`@0x160980): consumes the persisted KV value — a poisoned KV turns this into a **persistent crash-loop** (the daemon can never start again until the KV entry is removed).

The lease flag registered with api 1001 (`RegistHandler(1001, handler, lease=1)`@0x1a3bf8→`sub_376D00`@0x376d00) does not gate the crash: `EnableLease(1.0)` is called (`sub_3768C4`@0x3768c4 → `sub_376760`@0x376760), but the lease validity check `sub_42A3F8`@0x42a3f8 returns ALLOW when no lease is currently held and the request carries no lease token, and any legit holder's lease **auto-expires after 1.0 s** — so at most a 1-second wait is needed.

1	# Finding: AUD-demarcate-estop-rebind
2	
3	## Primitive
4	Auth / Access Control Bypass + Injection (binary-verified outcome of the bashrunner argument-injection chain: 6 attacker-controlled bytes persisted to a fixed root path — the wireless e-stop/handle RF pairing ID — plus unauthenticated motor-mask calibration commands; direct RCE via option/argument injection REFUTED at the binary layer)
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH (unauthenticated, remote (DDS/WiFi-AP/WebRTC-bridge) neutralization of the robot's wireless e-stop pairing + persistent robot-identity corruption + uncommanded motor calibration on attacker-chosen motors; NOT direct code execution)
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	This is the binary-level (LB-3) resolution of the escalation question left open by AUD-bashrunner-dds-root-exec and AUD-bashrunner-motortools-arginj: the unauthenticated DDS topic `rt/api/bashrunner/request` delivers attacker-controlled whitespace-free tokens as unquoted positional `$1` into 5 root scripts that invoke `basic_demarcate` / `basic_motorcali`. Full argv-parse reverse engineering of both binaries (IDA, functions cited below) shows:
13	
14	1. **No exec sink exists.** `basic_demarcate` imports exactly 44 undefined dynamic symbols (43 functions + `__stack_chk_guard`; verified: full `nm -D` enumeration — REVIEW-corrected from "46") — zero of system/exec/popen/fork/dlopen; `basic_motorcali` likewise has no process-creation import. The hidden `--cmd1..4` options (strings evidence) are NOT exec hooks: they map to `Command_mode_function(12..15)` (basic_demarcate@0x19c8), which merely sets a command-code byte (12-15) in a fixed 28-byte ZMQ frame sent to the local basic_service daemon over `ipc:///tmp/REQ.ipc` (basic_demarcate@0x29d8 zeromqREQSend). The tool's own help calls them "undetermined cmd1..4". They are not reachable from any whitelisted script anyway (no script passes them — argv[1] is fixed in all 14 live scripts; only the inert motortools.sh passes bare positionals and its target binary is absent from the image).
15	2. **No option-injection position exists.** `basic_demarcate@main` (0x2db4) switches on argc: only 1/2/3 are handled, argc>3 → `exit(-11)`; argv[1] is matched by exact strcmp against a fixed option table (.data 0x16020-0x16148, resolved via .rela.dyn: `--help --zerotorque --imucalibration --jointcalibration --setupwirelesshandleid --poweroffwirelesshandle --turnonwirelesshandle --machinetype --downwardankle --upwardsankle --clearonemotorerror --partmotorcali --cmd1..4 --auxiliarycalibration --estoppower` + short forms), and argv[2] is consumed as that option's typed VALUE inside `checkCommand_RfID_Flashlight` (0x21e8) — a token starting with `-` can never be re-parsed as an option. Glob word-multiplication of `$1` only produces argc>3 → clean exit. `basic_motorcali@main` (0x16460) uses boost::program_options typed values (`partmotorcali` = `value<std::string>()`); an attacker token in the value slot is consumed by `strtoul` (0x16a38 path) or throws an uncaught boost exception (process abort, no escalation).

158	bashrunner `split()`s it (whitespace-free tokens), checks the first token against its

161	value slot). `basic_demarcate@main` argc==3 + `strlen(argv[2])==6` gate the value, then
162	runs the 4-step sequence ("power on estop" → "set id estop" → "power on rf" → "set id rf",

# Finding: AUD-demarcate-estop-rebind

## Primitive
Auth / Access Control Bypass + Injection (binary-verified outcome of the bashrunner argument-injection chain: 6 attacker-controlled bytes persisted to a fixed root path — the wireless e-stop/handle RF pairing ID — plus unauthenticated motor-mask calibration commands; direct RCE via option/argument injection REFUTED at the binary layer)

## Severity
HIGH (unauthenticated, remote (DDS/WiFi-AP/WebRTC-bridge) neutralization of the robot's wireless e-stop pairing + persistent robot-identity corruption + uncommanded motor calibration on attacker-chosen motors; NOT direct code execution)

## Condition Analysis

### Summary
This is the binary-level (LB-3) resolution of the escalation question left open by AUD-bashrunner-dds-root-exec and AUD-bashrunner-motortools-arginj: the unauthenticated DDS topic `rt/api/bashrunner/request` delivers attacker-controlled whitespace-free tokens as unquoted positional `$1` into 5 root scripts that invoke `basic_demarcate` / `basic_motorcali`. Full argv-parse reverse engineering of both binaries (IDA, functions cited below) shows:

1. **No exec sink exists.** `basic_demarcate` imports exactly 44 undefined dynamic symbols (43 functions + `__stack_chk_guard`; verified: full `nm -D` enumeration — REVIEW-corrected from "46") — zero of system/exec/popen/fork/dlopen; `basic_motorcali` likewise has no process-creation import. The hidden `--cmd1..4` options (strings evidence) are NOT exec hooks: they map to `Command_mode_function(12..15)` (basic_demarcate@0x19c8), which merely sets a command-code byte (12-15) in a fixed 28-byte ZMQ frame sent to the local basic_service daemon over `ipc:///tmp/REQ.ipc` (basic_demarcate@0x29d8 zeromqREQSend). The tool's own help calls them "undetermined cmd1..4". They are not reachable from any whitelisted script anyway (no script passes them — argv[1] is fixed in all 14 live scripts; only the inert motortools.sh passes bare positionals and its target binary is absent from the image).
2. **No option-injection position exists.** `basic_demarcate@main` (0x2db4) switches on argc: only 1/2/3 are handled, argc>3 → `exit(-11)`; argv[1] is matched by exact strcmp against a fixed option table (.data 0x16020-0x16148, resolved via .rela.dyn: `--help --zerotorque --imucalibration --jointcalibration --setupwirelesshandleid --poweroffwirelesshandle --turnonwirelesshandle --machinetype --downwardankle --upwardsankle --clearonemotorerror --partmotorcali --cmd1..4 --auxiliarycalibration --estoppower` + short forms), and argv[2] is consumed as that option's typed VALUE inside `checkCommand_RfID_Flashlight` (0x21e8) — a token starting with `-` can never be re-parsed as an option. Glob word-multiplication of `$1` only produces argc>3 → clean exit. `basic_motorcali@main` (0x16460) uses boost::program_options typed values (`partmotorcali` = `value<std::string>()`); an attacker token in the value slot is consumed by `strtoul` (0x16a38 path) or throws an uncaught boost exception (process abort, no escalation).
3. **The value slots are strongly typed:** `--machinetype` requires strlen==1 and digit '1'-'9'; `--clearonemotorerror` requires atoi in [0,255]; `--partmotorcali` is any u64 (motor-enable bitmask, basic_demarcate@0x21e8 / basic_motorcali@0x242d0 setcalimotorid); **`--setupwirelesshandleid` requires strlen==6 and accepts ANY 6 non-whitespace bytes** (basic_demarcate@0x21e8: `dword_1623B = *(_DWORD*)argv[2]; word_1623F = *((_WORD*)argv[2]+2)`).
4. **What the values DO (the confirmed primitive):** `basic_demarcate --setupwirelesshandleid <6 chars>` (main@0x2db4 argc==3 branch) runs a 4-step sequence — power-on estop, **set estop ID = attacker's 6 bytes**, power-on RF, **set RF ID = the same 6 bytes** (change_rf_estopid@0x2d5c ×4). On each daemon OK-reply, `RF_Light_JointMotor` (0x2648) with `byte_161C0==254` calls `WirteReadFileCheck("/unitree/robot/basic/rfcode","w+","r+",&dword_1623B,6)` (0x3774→write_data_to_file@0x3548): **the attacker's 6 arbitrary bytes are persisted to `/unitree/robot/basic/rfcode` as root**. The write path is FIXED (path constants .data 0x161d0/0x161d8/0x16220 via .rela.dyn → 0x3b10/0x3b30/0x3c50) — no path traversal, no arbitrary file. The paired readback oracle exists: whitelisted `content_acquisition/get_rfcode.sh` = `sudo cat /unitree/robot/basic/rfcode`, and bashrunner returns script stdout on `rt/api/bashrunner/response` (bashrunner.py:107-128) — the attacker can read the current ID, overwrite it, and verify the new value. `--machinetype <d>` persists 1 digit byte to `/unitree/robot/basic/machinetype` (same write path, `byte_161C0==247`); `--poweroffwirelesshandle`/`--turnonwirelesshandle` persist "0"/"1" to `/unitree/robot/basic/rfpower` (`byte_161C0==251/252`). `basic_motorcali --partmotorcali <u64>` puts the mask into a fixed 28-byte ZMQ frame (ipctobasic_motorcali@0x24728 → executeCommand@0x246a0) commanding partial motor calibration on the attacker-chosen subset of the 35 motors.
5. **Memory corruption (E20) also refuted:** the only unsafe string helpers (`createDirectory`@0x32d0 — 256-byte stack buffer, unbounded strlen copy; `getpath`@0x3174 — sprintf+strcat into a 512-byte heap buffer) have ZERO xrefs (dead code, verified via xrefs_to). Every reachable buffer is bounded: `RfIDStringToData`@0x2074 loops strlen but `RfDataConversion`@0x1f50 writes only for indices 1,2,3,5 into fixed in-frame fields; the estop ID copy reads/writes exactly 6 bytes into adjacent globals; all ZMQ frames are fixed 28 bytes with CRC16.

**Net verdict for the E2-rce cell:** the DDS→bashrunner→root-binary chain does NOT close as direct RCE — the binaries are pure "build fixed frame → ZMQ IPC to basic_service → optionally persist 1-6 bytes to one of three fixed config files" tools. The maximum damage is (a) **e-stop/handle pairing rebind to attacker-chosen ID** (the operator's physical remote stops matching the robot — safety-device neutralization), (b) robot-identity/config corruption (machinetype, rfpower, rfcode persisted), (c) **uncommanded physical actuation** (zero torque, joint/IMU/ankle calibration, motor calibration on an attacker-selected motor mask — physical impact already filed as AUD-bashrunner-robot-state), (d) root process aborts (uncaught boost exceptions) — a root-crash nuisance only.

### Pre-conditions
- All pre-conditions of AUD-bashrunner-dds-root-exec (unauthenticated DDS publish with shipped etc/ds/ identity + mock_sender.py QoS; or WebRTC data-channel bridge).
- bashrunner running as root (master_service `bashrunner` service config) and `basic_service` running (it is a core service, etc/master_service/service/basic_service → module/basic_service/run.sh → the `ipc:///tmp/REQ.ipc` ZMQ REP daemon; 5.8MB Virbox/runner-wrapped, present in image).
- For the rfcode WRITE specifically: the estop/RF setid command must succeed daemon-side (estop module attached and powered) — `RF_Light_JointMotor` writes only on an OK reply (byte_16173==1 + 20-byte frame echo + CRC match, zeromqREQRev@0x2a54). The ID CHANGE command itself is sent unconditionally.
- For the e-stop-rebind impact: robot's wireless handle/e-stop in use (standard configuration).

### Data Flow
1. Attacker publishes `{"script": "demarcate_setup_wireless_handle_id.sh <6 chars>"}` (or `basic_motorcali_partmotorcali.sh <u64>`, `demarcate_partmotorcali.sh <u64>`, `demarcate_setup_machine_type.sh <d>`, `demarcate_clearonemotorerror.sh <int>`) on rt/api/bashrunner/request.
   Application: bashrunner.py:90-91 json.loads + split; :98 whitelist; :102-106 `subprocess.run(["sh", script, tok])` as root.
2. Script forwards the token as the fixed option's value: `sudo /unitree/robot/tool/basic_demarcate --setupwirelesshandleid $1` (demarcate_setup_wireless_handle_id.sh:1) — unquoted `$1` (glob-capable, but >1 glob match ⇒ argc>3 ⇒ exit(-11); exactly one word lands in the value slot).
3. basic_demarcate@0x2db4 main: argc==3 → argv[1] strcmp-matched (--setupwirelesshandleid / 0x3948), strlen(argv[2])==6 gate → 4× change_rf_estopid (0x2d5c) = checkCommand_RfID_Flashlight (0x21e8) → Command_mode_function (0x19c8, sets byte_161C0=254 for setid) → RfIDStringToData (0x2074, converts the 6 chars into the frame) → zeromqREQSend (0x29d8, fixed 28-byte frame to ipc:///tmp/REQ.ipc) → zeromqREQRev (0x2a54) → RF_Light_JointMotor (0x2648).
4. On daemon OK: WirteReadFileCheck("/unitree/robot/basic/rfcode", "w+", "r+", &dword_1623B, 6) (0x3774) → write_data_to_file (0x3548) → createDirectory+fopen+fwrite — the attacker's 6 bytes persisted as root at the fixed path.
5. Attacker verifies via `{"script": "get_rfcode.sh"}` → `sudo cat /unitree/robot/basic/rfcode` → stdout returned on rt/api/bashrunner/response (bashrunner.py:107-128).

### Taint Trace
```
Source: sample.parameter {"script": "demarcate_setup_wireless_handle_id.sh ABC123"} at bashrunner.py:90
  (DDS rt/api/bashrunner/request, unauthenticated — AUD-bashrunner-dds-root-exec)

    command_execution/demarcate_setup_wireless_handle_id.sh:1 — unquoted $1 = value slot
    (glob multiplication would only push argc>3 → basic_demarcate@0x2db4 exit(-11))

    Guard: VALUE TYPING — strlen(argv[2])==6 exact; argv[1] fixed by script ⇒ NO option

  → daemon OK reply → RF_Light_JointMotor byte_161C0==254 at basic_demarcate@0x2648

Vulnerability class: Auth bypass (unauthenticated privileged RPC) → safety-state corruption /
persistent config write (fixed-path, bounded-content) — NOT command injection, NOT memory corruption

### Guard Assessment

### Strategy

Reuse the robot's own shipped client for this exact topic —
`module/bashrunner/mock_sender.py:20-30` — because its QoS is load-bearing: the
bashrunner reader asks Reliable + Deadline(1000 µs) + TransientLocal + KeepLast(10), and a
default BestEffort/Volatile writer will **not** match. The whole attack is one DDS message
whose `parameter` is `{"script": "demarcate_setup_wireless_handle_id.sh <6 chars>"}`:
bashrunner `split()`s it (whitespace-free tokens), checks the first token against its
`os.listdir()` whitelist, and runs `sh <script> <token>` as root; the script body is
`sudo /unitree/robot/tool/basic_demarcate --setupwirelesshandleid $1` (unquoted `$1` = the
value slot). `basic_demarcate@main` argc==3 + `strlen(argv[2])==6` gate the value, then
runs the 4-step sequence ("power on estop" → "set id estop" → "power on rf" → "set id rf",
each a fixed 28-byte ZMQ frame to `ipc:///tmp/REQ.ipc`), and on each daemon OK reply
persists the 6 raw bytes to the FIXED path `/unitree/robot/basic/rfcode`. The same topic
is a readback oracle: whitelisted `get_rfcode.sh` = `sudo cat /unitree/robot/basic/rfcode`
and bashrunner returns script stdout on `rt/api/bashrunner/response` (bashrunner.py:107-128).
Because this is a **safety primitive** (it rebinds the operator's wireless e-stop/handle
pairing), the write leg is gated behind `--execute` and defaults to re-writing the value
just read — a no-op rebind that exercises the full 4-step write path with zero net state
change. An attacker passes their own 6 bytes.

### Prerequisites

- `cyclonedds` 0.10.2 bindings + shipped DDS identity + LAN reachability.
- Offline mode: Python 3.8+, no deps — replays the argv/binary semantics in a sandbox.
- Live robot: bashrunner + basic_service running (both ship enabled, both root).
- For the file write to occur: the estop/RF setid command must get an OK reply from
  basic_service (normal on a provisioned robot — the ID-change command is sent regardless).

def sh_word_split(line, root):
    """`sh script $token`: unquoted $1 word-splits + glob-expands before exec."""
    words = []
    for tok in line.split()[1:]:
        if "*" in tok or "?" in tok:
            import glob as g
            words.extend(g.glob(os.path.join(root, tok)) or [tok])  # nullglob off -> literal

    root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="poc-basic-")
    rf = os.path.join(root, "rfcode")

    print("   ", bashrunner({"script": "get_rfcode.sh"}, rf, root))
    print("[2] VALUE GATES (harness) — all of these leave rfcode untouched:")

        print(f"[4] WRITE LEG (harness, id={new!r}):")
        print(f"    -> {bashrunner({'script': f'{SCRIPT} {new}'}, rf, root)}")
        print(f"    readback: {bashrunner({'script': 'get_rfcode.sh'}, rf, root)}")
    else:

if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--mode", choices=["offline", "dds"], default="offline")
    ap.add_argument("--execute", action="store_true",

    ap.add_argument("--wait", type=float, default=6.0)

1	# Finding: AUD-robottype-traversal-copy
2	
3	## Primitive
4	File Upload / Path Traversal (arbitrary-source recursive copy + fixed-destination overwrite as root) — chain class: **config corruption / machine-variant swap / filesystem exhaustion**, not direct RCE.
5	
6	## Severity
7	HIGH (unauthenticated, remote, root-privileged file-replacement primitive over the robot's machine-config directory; honest bound: no code-exec consumer found — see Impact)
8	
9	## Condition Analysis
10	
11	### Summary
12	`robot_type_api_server` (root daemon, `etc/master_service/service/robot_type_service`, started via start-stop-daemon as root) exposes four unauthenticated DDS RPC handlers on `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` registered by `RobotTypeServer::Init@0x830a8` at `../api/robot_type_server.cpp:24-27` with `RegistHandler(apiId, fn, /*lease=*/false)` (verified: `mov w3, #0` before each `bl RegistHandler@0xa4098`). Handler 1002 `Set_Robot_Type@0x84ea8` parses a JSON parameter whose sole field is `{"version": <string>}` (`Set_Robot_Type_Parameter::fromJson`, `robot_type_server_api.hpp:58`, field name string at 0x169d08) with **no validation of any kind**, then at `robot_type_server.cpp:89` calls `copyVersionSourceFiles@0x824e0(version)`. That function builds `source = "/unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_source_file" + "/" + version` (constant @0x1695b0 + separator "/" @0x1695f0, `robot_type_server.cpp:163`), checks only that the source exists (`fs::exists` @:168 via `fs::status` PLT@0x52c80), then at `:174` calls `std::filesystem::create_directories("/unitree/robot/basic")` (PLT@0x53840) and at `:177` calls `std::filesystem::copy(source, "/unitree/robot/basic", std::filesystem::copy_options(0xA))` (`mov w2, #10` @0x82764, throwing overload PLT@0x54a50) — **as root**. Because `version` is concatenated verbatim, any `../` sequence traverses: `{"version":"../../../<any path>"}` makes the copy source any readable file or directory on the filesystem while the destination stays the fixed `/unitree/robot/basic`. The shipped `robot_type_source_file/` contains only `1/` and `2/` (each `basic_motor.json`, `basic_service.json`, `machinetype`) — i.e. the "version" is normally a one-character machine-variant id, and the API is a factory provisioning hook exposed on the network.
13	
14	The exact copy semantics were verified by disassembling the shipped `module/r1_arm_example/lib/libstdc++.so.6.0.34` `std::filesystem::copy(const path&, const path&, copy_options, error_code&)` @0x132a5c:
15	- `copy_options 0xA` = `recursive(8) | overwrite_existing(2)` (libstdc++ `copy_options` bit layout: none=0, skip_existing=1, overwrite_existing=2, update_existing=4, recursive=8, copy_symlinks=0x10, skip_symlinks=0x20, directories_only=0x40, create_symlinks=0x80, create_hard_links=0x100).
16	- Because `(options & 0xB0) == 0`, the source is statted with **`stat()`**, not `lstat()` (0x132a98 `b.eq` → 0x132ad0 `bl stat`) — **symlinks in the source path are followed and the target's CONTENT is copied**, not the link.
17	- **Single-file source**: at 0x132c20-0x132c94 the code computes `from.filename()` (0x132c34) then `to / from.filename()` (0x132c44 `operator/`) and calls `do_copy_file(from, to/from.filename(), …)`. So **a single file source IS planted into `/unitree/robot/basic/` under its own basename** — this answers hunt-item #1 affirmatively.
18	- **Directory source**: 0x132cf0 `tbnz w20,#3` (recursive) → 0x132e8c; if `to` absent → `create_directory(to, from)` (0x132cfc), then a `directory_iterator` loop at 0x132d94-0x132df4 that calls `fs::copy(entry.path(), to / entry.path().filename(), options)` for **every** entry. There is **no symlink-skip check in the loop**, and the recursive call passes the same options (0xA) so `stat()` is used again — symlinks inside a copied tree are dereferenced and their target content planted.
19	- `equivalent(from, to)` → `EEXIST` error (0x132b88); `from` dir + `to` regular file → `EISDIR` (0x132bcc). Both raise `filesystem_error`.
20	- Errors do **not** crash the daemon: `copyVersionSourceFiles` has its own `try/catch` (landing pad at 0x82e54 = `__cxa_begin_catch`, `robot_type_server.cpp:183-185`, log string "拷贝版本{}源文件异常: {}" @0x1696d0) and `Set_Robot_Type` has a second one (0x8571c, `:103-108`, "Set_Robot_Type异常: {}" @0x169ac0). 21	
22	### Pre-conditions
23	- Attacker can publish to the DDS topic `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` (any LAN peer on 192.168.123.0/24 — cyclonedds.xml binds DDS to eth0; per scratchboard reachability correction the robot's own wlan1 AP subnet does *not* reach DDS), **or** rides the WebRTC data channel: `rt/api/robot_type_service/request` is a registered bridge publisher and `.../response` a registered subscriber (`var/log/webrtc_bridge/webrtc_bridge.LOG:5402` and `:5432`), and the shipped log contains live production traffic on this exact topic — `webrtc_bridge.LOG:6344`: `{"type":"req","topic":"rt/api/robot_type_service/request","data":{"header":{"identity":{"id":3,"api_id":1001}},"parameter":"{\"version\":\"\"}"}}` (2026-07-20 16:05:27). 31	   `{"header":{"identity":{"id":1,"api_id":1002}},"parameter":"{\"version\":\"../../../unitree\"}"}`
32	   Application: `ServerStub::QueueThreadFunction@0xace48` → handler table → `Set_Robot_Type@0x84ea8` (`robot_type_server.cpp:60` "调用Set_Robot_Type API").

36	5. `robot_type_server.cpp:163` — `source = "/unitree/module/robot_type_service/robot_type_source_file/../../../unitree"` (resolves to `/unitree`).

40	   - `{"version":"../../../robot/basic"}` → `equivalent(from,to)` → `EEXIST` → caught → `code:-1`. (Harmless — listed to show the guard.)
